stamp.title: Approve $11,880.00 refund and corrected invoice
stamp.reason: Invoice is $11,880.00 above the signed agreement.

checks.label: Bias
checks.question: Is the wording one-sided?
checks.answer: The complaint is firm and threatens media and legal action. The word 'fraud' is the customer's allegation, not a finding.

checks.label: Accuracy
checks.question: Do the numbers and claims match the documents?
checks.answer: The invoice contradicts the agreement. The overcharge claim is supported. The fraud and other-customers claims are not shown in the documents.

checks.label: Misleading
checks.question: Does anything give a wrong impression?
checks.answer: The invoice note says rush applied because work finished within 30 days. Clause 4 requires a written rush request. An internal message suggests stalling clients.

quotes.text: Rush tier applied because processing was completed within 30 days of collection.
If the Customer has not made a written rush request, the standard rate in clause 3 applies.
most of them give up if we stall for a month

checks.label: Governance
checks.question: What should happen next, and under which rule?
checks.answer: Personal information was shared by email after the accounts team asked for it. A fraud allegation and an internal message need review by the Complaints Manager, not the accounts team.

manage.label: Refund
manage.text: Hold the invoice, confirm clause 4 was not triggered, then issue the corrected invoice and refund. Billing Manager approves; Finance Director too, over $10,000.

manage.label: Privacy
manage.text: Restrict the thread to the complaints team and Privacy Officer. Report the exposure within 1 business day. Stop asking customers to email identity details.

manage.label: Conduct
manage.text: Refer the fraud allegation and the internal message to the Complaints Manager. The accounts team should not handle it.
